title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
This incident shows a failure of post-incident data transparency for a deployed driver-assist system. The system detected a hazard before the fatal crash, but the company initially said no crash data existed. Independent recovery through a bug bounty program showed the data was present. The failure occurred after deployment, in the investigation and accountability stage, not in the model's real-time driving decision.

Catching this would have required independent verification of the vehicle's data storage before accepting the company's claim. A third-party audit or direct access to the vehicle's logs could have shown the data existed. The absence of such a check allowed a false claim about missing data to stand until a hacker recovered it.

What is not established is whether the initial claim of missing data was deliberate. The jury's verdict establishes partial responsibility and damages, but the reports do not prove intent to conceal.

summary:
A 2024 Tesla crash killed one person and injured another, leading to a lawsuit against the company. Tesla initially claimed it had no crash data from the incident, but a Russian hacker working through Tesla's bug bounty program recovered the data and proved the company did possess it. A jury found Tesla partially responsible and ordered the company to pay 243 million dollars in damages. The case raised concerns about Tesla's transparency regarding autonomous vehicle crashes and its safety claims.

The incident has broader implications as Tesla prepares to launch fully autonomous Cybercabs. Recent data shows Tesla vehicles with active driver-assist systems were involved in 207 crashes in May alone, the highest number recorded. A coach was injured in a Tesla on autopilot this month, and federal regulators have escalated an investigation into potential self-driving software failures. These ongoing safety concerns and questions about data transparency suggest caution may be warranted as the company rolls out its fully autonomous vehicles.
